placements.why: The document's core move — an aphorism equating unrehearsed rollback with no rollback at all, backing a directive to rehearse monthly — names an organizational stance that capability must be proven through practice rather than assumed from design or documentation. Nothing in the (empty) existing strata covers this category of organizational concern, and the content is foundational enough (a stance on what counts as 'having' a capability) to stand as its own top-level category rather than a child of something else.
placements.title: Capability claims are settled by demonstration, not declaration
placements.frame: Does this content establish a practice or process whose purpose is to convert a claimed capability into a verified one through repeated demonstration?

placements.title: Rollback capability is sustained by a recurring rehearsal cadence, not a one-time build
placements.frame: Is the expression here formalizing rehearsal as an ongoing, scheduled operational practice — a cadence with an owner — rather than a single completed task?
placements.why: src-1's directive ('run monthly from now on'), src-3's restatement of the cadence as a structured field, and src-4's owner assignment together constitute a single recurring theme: the rollback capability is kept alive by an ongoing scheduled practice with a named accountable party, not a one-time setup. This is a subject future envelopes about Atlas (or other systems') rehearsal logs, misses, or cadence changes will keep feeding — a genuine narrative leaf, not a fact. The owner and cadence fields are the formalization of the same commitment src-1 announces, so they support this leaf rather than minting separate leaves for the metadata fields themselves.

placements.title: A capability is defined by its demonstrated exercise, not its nominal or designed existence
placements.frame: Does the expression treat an unrehearsed capability as effectively absent — collapsing the distinction between 'built' and 'proven' — rather than treating rehearsal as merely a best practice?
placements.why: src-2's aphorism ('a rollback we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have') states a principle that goes beyond this one Atlas cadence decision: it asserts a general equivalence between demonstrated practice and actual possession of a capability. This is a stance the org can invoke again for any capability, not a fact bound to this envelope's Atlas decision — distinct from the cadence-formalization theme, since it is the justificatory premise rather than the operational schedule itself.
